scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field manual-read route completion was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9,200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: Dispute-ticket response times are median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA, across 2,440 tickets.

F-03.statement: CRM dispute volume rose from 610 (2026-06) and 590 (2026-07) to 1180 (2026-08) and 1260 (2026-09), roughly doubling from the Jun-Jul baseline.

F-04.statement: Of disputed bills, 1785 had read_type ACTUAL and 1240 had read_type ESTIMATED (3025 total).

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 states the utility may request route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-SLOW-RESPONSE-AUTOMATABLE.statement: The August-September dispute surge stems from inadequate ticket response capacity/speed, and both auto-answering tickets and auto-correcting bills via an AI agent will resolve it.

H-AMI-MDMS-PIPELINE-FAILURE.statement: AMI read delivery or MDMS validation began failing or degrading around August, producing bad/estimated reads that generated incorrect bills and drove the dispute surge.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual field meter reading completion dropped or became unreliable around August, forcing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills, independent of ticket handling speed.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (e.g., read-type acceptance or estimate logic) around August introduced systematic bill errors that drove the dispute surge.

H-BILL-ACCURACY-UNCHANGED-PERC.statement: Bills remain as accurate as before August and the ticket surge reflects customer reaction to a rate/tariff or billing-cycle change rather than any pipeline or process defect.

H-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR.statement: A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carried an ACTUAL read type rather than ESTIMATED, suggesting incorrect actual meter reads (field or AMI-sourced) being accepted into billing may be a larger driver of disputes than estimate substitution.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: The field reading contractor has been short three readers since July, causing manual-read routes to run behind schedule and forcing estimate substitution for affected accounts, driving part of the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log shows manual-read route completion of only 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts during Aug-Sep 2026, i.e. a real shortfall in field meter-read collection coinciding with the dispute surge window. This points to a tangible process gap (missed manual reads forcing estimate substitution) rather than merely a ticket-handling or tariff-perception issue.

CRM data shows dispute-ticket response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are already within the 3.0-day SLA across 2,440 tickets, so ticket-handling speed is not a bottleneck in the current surge; the problem is not that staff respond too slowly.

CRM dispute-volume data shows roughly a doubling of monthly disputes (≈600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 to ≈1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026), confirming the magnitude and timing of the surge described in the initial request, but it carries no information about the underlying cause.

Billing-db shows disputed bills split 1785 ACTUAL vs 1240 ESTIMATED read type (3025 total), i.e. the majority of disputed bills carried an ACTUAL read, not an ESTIMATED one — estimate substitution accounts for only ~41% of disputed bills.

Billing-db's tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff/rate change was logged around the dispute surge; this rules out a tariff change as the driver and specifically undercuts the tariff-change clause of H-BILL-ACCURACY-UNCHANGED-PERC.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that there has been no tariff change this year is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that agrees with the already-recorded authoritative finding (E-05) that no tariff change occurred during the surge; it adds no new decision-relevant information beyond corroborating that record.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims the field reading team has been short three readers since July, causing manual-read routes to run late and those customers to receive estimated bills instead. This is a non-authoritative stakeholder explanation for the route completion shortfall, not independently verified, and comes from a stakeholder with a stated incentive toward headcount increase and a bias toward attributing problems to staffing.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract (§4.2) confirms that while the utility may request route priority changes, execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager — this is the authoritative basis for the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update and for success criterion SC-NO-UNCONFIRMED-DISPATCH-CHAN. It does not speak to the cause of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query returned 320 accounts with an estimated read in the last billing cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (account_id, route fields). This reveals billing-db records carry a 'route' field, which is a potential join key with route-log data that the plan had treated as unconfirmed/absent for cross-source correlation.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log lagging_routes query returns 14 distinct routes each with its own completion rate (sample: route R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity under the aggregate 88% manual-read completion shortfall; it contains no cause (staffing or otherwise) for the lateness.

U-ROOT-MECHANISM-UNRESOLVED.question: Is the mechanism producing erroneous ACTUAL meter reads an AMI/MDMS pipeline failure, a billing import validation rule change, or field meter-reading error?
U-ROOT-MECHANISM-UNRESOLVED.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation must target the AMI vendor pipeline, a billing-config rule rollback, or field reading QA, and whether any fix requires a protected write under K-BILLWRITE.
U-ROOT-MECHANISM-UNRESOLVED.resolution_path: Obtain the vendor-provisioned MDMS AMI read event export (currently ACCESS_PENDING per recovery log) and review the billing-config rule change log for the August 2026 period.
U-ROOT-MECHANISM-UNRESOLVED.safe_placeholder: Continue manual review/flagging of disputed ACTUAL-read accounts; do not deploy any automated billing fix until the root mechanism is confirmed.

U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-UNVERI.question: How much of the ESTIMATED-read dispute minority is actually explained by the field staffing shortage SH-FIELD describes, versus other causes?
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-UNVERI.decision_impact: Affects whether any dispatch or staffing remediation is warranted and in what proportion relative to the ACTUAL-read mechanism.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-UNVERI.resolution_path: Cross-reference route-log completion/staffing trends against the ESTIMATED-read subset of disputed bills.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-UNVERI.safe_placeholder: Treat SH-FIELD's staffing explanation as unverified; take no dispatch or headcount action on it alone.

U-METRIC-DECOMPOSITION-VALIDIT.question: Does aggregate monthly dispute volume alone validly measure resolution, given disputes split across ACTUAL-read and ESTIMATED-read causes with likely different fixes and timelines?
U-METRIC-DECOMPOSITION-VALIDIT.decision_impact: Determines whether success tracking must decompose dispute volume by read type rather than relying on a single aggregate baseline figure.
U-METRIC-DECOMPOSITION-VALIDIT.resolution_path: Track dispute volume decomposed by read type (ACTUAL vs ESTIMATED) alongside the aggregate trend.
U-METRIC-DECOMPOSITION-VALIDIT.safe_placeholder: Report both the aggregate and the read-type-decomposed dispute trend until decomposition is validated.

A-UPSTREAM-READ-DEFECT-SOURCE.statement: The erroneous ACTUAL reads are assumed to originate from an upstream read/validation defect (field reading, AMI telemetry, or MDMS validation) rather than a billing calculation error, though the exact source among AMI/MDMS pipeline failure or a billing rule change is not yet confirmed.

A-FIELD-STAFFING-MINORITY-CONT.statement: Field staffing shortage (SH-FIELD's claim) is assumed to be a plausible but unverified contributor to the smaller ESTIMATED-read portion of disputes, since it comes from a non-authoritative, potentially biased source.
